s1.syndrome_frame: Palpitations and shortness of breath with a history of arrhythmia
salient_findings: Regular rhythm with cannon A waves in the jugular venous waveform
Incomplete right bundle branch block morphology on ECG
key_facts: 20-year history of palpitations and shortness of breath
Episodes were previously controlled with verapamil
Sustained symptoms recurred 6 months before presentation
Not responding to amiodarone therapy
Heart rate: 122 beats per minute
Blood pressure: 135/85 mm Hg
ECG shows regular tachycardia at 130 beats per minute
QRS duration of 118 milliseconds
Left-axis deviation on ECG
3:2 relationship between ventricular and atrial activations
24-hour Holter monitor showed sustained tachycardia throughout monitoring period
Echocardiogram results within normal limits

shortlist.label: Atrioventricular Nodal Reentrant Tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Regular tachycardia with 3:2 relationship between ventricular and atrial activations, consistent with AVNRT

shortlist.label: Orthodromic Atrioventricular Reentrant Tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Sustained tachycardia with left-axis deviation and incomplete right bundle branch block morphology, suggestive of orthodromic AVRT

shortlist.label: Atrial Flutter
shortlist.why_kept: Regular tachycardia with negative deflection in leads II and aVF, consistent with atrial flutter

shortlist.label: Supraventricular Tachycardia with Aberrancy
shortlist.why_kept: Tachycardia with aberrant conduction, as evidenced by the 3:2 relationship and left-axis deviation

shortlist.label: Wolff-Parkinson-White Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: History of palpitations and shortness of breath, with ECG findings consistent with pre-excitation syndrome

raw.rationale: The patient's ECG shows a regular tachycardia with a 3:2 relationship between ventricular and atrial activations, and the presence of cannon A waves in the jugular venous waveform, which is consistent with Atrioventricular Nodal Reentrant Tachycardia. The patient's history of response to verapamil also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Orthodromic Atrioventricular Reentrant Tachycardia
rejected.why: This condition typically involves an accessory pathway and would likely show pre-excitation on the ECG, which is not mentioned.

rejected.label: Atrial Flutter
rejected.why: Atrial Flutter typically shows a sawtooth pattern on the ECG, which is not described in the vignette.

rejected.label: Supraventricular Tachycardia with Aberrancy
rejected.why: This condition would likely show a wider QRS complex due to the aberrancy, but the QRS duration is 118 milliseconds, which is not significantly wide.

rejected.label: Wolff-Parkinson-White Syndrome
rejected.why: This condition typically shows pre-excitation on the ECG, which is not mentioned in the vignette.
